description:
We are a passionate team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, combining frontend development, backend development, and UI/UX design.

We aim to use our technical and creative skills to explore NASA's open data and build an innovative, interactive, and meaningful solution.

We enjoy solving problems, learning, experimenting, and turning ideas into working projects.
summary:
The Silent Legacy is an interactive 2D pixel-art experience that explores the stories of human-made machines and equipment left behind during space exploration on the Moon and Mars.

By combining pixel-art environments with real NASA imagery and mission information, the project creates an engaging way for people to discover the history and significance of these abandoned artifacts.

The project uses NASA's Images API to incorporate real space exploration photographs and the NSSDCA Catalog to provide historical mission information. Through an accessible visual storytelling experience, we aim to connect audiences with the legacy of space exploration and raise awareness of the human-made objects that remain beyond Earth.
details:
What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

The Silent Legacy allows users to explore abandoned space exploration machines and artifacts through an interactive 2D pixel-art environment. Users can discover different locations on the Moon and Mars, interact with individual artifacts, and access information about their missions, historical backgrounds, and scientific contributions.

The project integrates NASA's Images API to retrieve real space exploration photographs and the NSSDCA Catalog to provide historical mission information. These resources help connect the visual experience with authentic NASA mission data.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Our goal is to make space exploration history more accessible, engaging, and enjoyable to discover. By presenting historical information through an interactive environment rather than conventional articles or static presentations, we hope to encourage curiosity about space science and technology.

The project also highlights the lasting significance of human-made objects beyond Earth, reminding audiences that even after missions end, their contributions remain part of humanity's exploration history.

Tools and Technologies

We developed the project using:

  • React for building the interactive user interface.
  • Vite for the development environment and build tooling.
  • CSS for custom visual effects and presentation.
  • NASA Images API for space exploration imagery.
  • NASA NSSDCA Catalog for historical spacecraft and mission information.

AI-assisted development and visual design tools were also used to support our development workflow.

Creativity and Innovation

Our creative approach combines educational content with a 2D pixel-art exploration environment. Rather than simply presenting a collection of historical facts, we wanted users to discover space artifacts through visual interaction.

The pixel-art aesthetic gives the experience a distinctive identity while making the subject approachable to a wider audience. Combining stylized environments with real NASA imagery also creates a connection between an imaginative visual presentation and authentic space exploration history.

Team Considerations

Throughout development, our team considered educational value, historical accuracy, accessibility, visual consistency, technical feasibility, and the limited time available during the hackathon.

We prioritized creating a functional and engaging experience while keeping the implementation manageable. We also focused on using publicly accessible NASA resources to ensure that the information presented was connected to real space exploration missions.

Explore The Silent Legacy through our publicly accessible live deployment:
